title: 2020年9月四级真题 第2套 阅读1
paperTitle: 2020年9月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
passage:
P1 When was cleaning a crime? When you're doing it to create art, obviously. A number of street artists around the world have started expressing themselves through a practice known as reverse graffiti(涂鸦). They find dirty surfaces and paint them with images or messages using cleaning brushes or pressure hoses(高压水管). Either way, it's the same principle: the image is made by cleaning away the dirt. Each artist has their own individual style but all artists share a common aim: to draw attention to the pollution in our cities. The UK's Paul Curtis, better known as Moose, operates around Leeds and London and has been commissioned by a number of companies to make reverse graffiti advertisements.

P2 Brazilian artist, Alexandre Orion, turned one of Sao Paulo's transport tunnels into an amazing wall painting in 2006 by getting rid of the dirt. Made up of a series of white skulls(颅骨), the painting reminds drivers of the effect their pollution is having on the planet. "Every motorist sits in the comfort of their car, but they don't give any consideration to the price their comfort has for the environment and consequently for themselves," says Orion.

P3 The anti-pollution message of the reverse graffiti artists confuses city authorities since the main argument against graffiti is that it spoils the appearance of both types of property: public and private. This was what Leeds City Council said about Moose's work: "Leeds residents want to live in clean and attractive neighbourhoods. We view this kind of advertising as environmental damage and will take strong action against it." Moose was ordered to "clean up his act." How was he supposed to do this: by making all property he had cleaned dirty again?

P4 As for the Brazilian artist's work, the authorities were annoyed but could find nothing to charge him with. They had no other option but to clean the tunnel—but only the parts Alexandre had already cleaned. The artist merely continued his campaign on the other side. The city officials then decided to take drastic action. They not only cleaned the whole tunnel but every tunnel in Sao Paulo.

questions.q: What do we learn from the passage about reverse graffiti?
options: It uses paint to create anti-pollution images.
It creates a lot of trouble for local residents.
It causes lots of distraction to drivers.
It turns dirty walls into artistic works.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do we learn from the passage about reverse graffiti? 问的是关于这个概念 的客观信息，答案应该是对原文某句的同义转述，不需要推断

【拆句】题干 What do we learn from the passage about reverse graffiti? 是 What 引导的特殊 疑问句，主干 we learn，from the passage 是状语，about reverse graffiti 修饰 learn 的 内容；无从句、无否定、无比较，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱 46. What do we learn from the passage about reverse graffiti? A) It uses paint to create anti-pollution images. B) It creates a lot of trouble for local residents. C) It causes lots of distraction to drivers. D) It turns dirty walls into artistic works.

【定位】They find dirty surfaces and paint them with images or messages using cleaning brushes or pressure hoses. Either way, it's the same principle: the image is made by cleaning away the dirt. 他们找到脏污的表面，用清洁刷或高压水管在上面「画」出图像或讯息。无论哪种方式，原 理都一样：图像是通过清除脏污而形成的。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 uses paint to create anti-pollution images 把原文的核心做法说反了——反向涂鸦恰 恰不用颜料，而是清除污渍 B) 无中生有 creates a lot of trouble for local residents 文中无对应描述；麻烦的是市议会的执法 逻辑，居民层面文中只提到他们 want to live in clean and attractive neighbourhoods，并未说反向涂鸦给居民带来麻烦 C) 张冠李戴 原文提到的是 Made up of a series of white skulls(颅骨), the painting reminds drivers of the effect their pollution is having on the planet——是提醒司机，而非 分散司机注意力；且这是 Orion 一人的做法，并非反向涂鸦的普遍特征 D) ✓ 正确 the image is made by cleaning away the dirt ↔turns dirty walls into artistic works 预判要的是「在脏面上靠清洁形成图像」，turns dirty walls into artistic works 正是这 层意思的同义改写 反向涂鸦艺术家试图做什么? A) 宣传他们的艺术追求。 B) 美化城市环境。 C) 提高公众对环境污染的意识。 D) 表达他们对地方政府的不满。

questions.q: What do reverse graffiti artists try to do?
options: Publicise their artistic pursuit.
Beautify the city environment.
Raise public awareness of environmental pollution.
Express their dissatisfaction with local governments.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do reverse graffiti artists try to do? 问群体共同意图，原文必有明文交代，仅 需找出该明文即可

【拆句】题干 What do reverse graffiti artists try to do? 是 What 引导的特殊疑问句，主语 reverse graffiti artists，谓语 try to do；try to do 是固定结构，表示「试图、致力于做某 事」；句法平直，无陷阱 47. What do reverse graffiti artists try to do? A) Publicise their artistic pursuit. B) Beautify the city environment. C) Raise public awareness of environmental pollution. D) Express their dissatisfaction with local governments.

【定位】Each artist has their own individual style but all artists share a common aim: to draw attention to the pollution in our cities. 每个艺术家都有自己独特的风格，但所有艺术家都拥有一个共同的目标：唤起人们对城市污 染的关注。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 Publicise their artistic pursuit 把原文中的「让公众关注城市污染」偷换成「宣传他们 自己的艺术追求」——原文 a common aim 是污染议题，不是他们个人艺术名声 B) 无中生有 Beautify the city environment 文中无对应；尽管反向涂鸦的产物确实清洁了表面，但 艺术家自陈的目的是「让人关注污染」，而非「美化城市」 C) ✓ 正确 to draw attention to the pollution in our cities ↔ Raise public awareness of environmental pollution 预判要的是「让公众关注污染」，Raise public awareness of environmental pollution 是其标准同义改写 D) 过度推断 Express their dissatisfaction with local governments 把作者在第三段对市议会的暗 讽错当成全体反向涂鸦艺术家的目的；原文意图句仅指向污染议题，并未把矛头对准 政府 关于巴西艺术家Alexandre Orion我们了解到什么? A) 他擅长绘制白色骷髅。 B) 他选择隧道来进行涂鸦艺术创作。 C) 他建议禁止所有污染汽车。 D) 他喜欢进行创意艺术创作。

questions.q: What do we learn about Brazilian artist Alexandre Orion?
options: He was good at painting white skulls.
He chose tunnels to do his graffiti art.
He suggested banning all polluting cars.
He was fond of doing creative artworks.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do we learn about Brazilian artist Alexandre Orion? 问的是该人物的客观情 况，属于以人为锚的细节题

【拆句】题干 What do we learn about Brazilian artist Alexandre Orion? 主干 we learn，about 后跟同位语结构「Brazilian artist Alexandre Orion」，前者是身份、后者是姓名；结构清 晰，无陷阱 48. What do we learn about Brazilian artist Alexandre Orion? A) He was good at painting white skulls. B) He chose tunnels to do his graffiti art. C) He suggested banning all polluting cars. D) He was fond of doing creative artworks.

【定位】Brazilian artist, Alexandre Orion, turned one of Sao Paulo's transport tunnels into an amazing wall painting in 2006 by getting rid of the dirt. 巴西艺术家亚历山大·奥利安在 2006 年通过清除污渍，把圣保罗的一条交通隧道变成了一幅 令人惊叹的壁画。

【选项】A) 过度推断 was good at painting white skulls 把原文中作品的视觉成分 a series of white skulls 误说成「擅长画白颅骨」；原文从未评价他的技能水平，颅骨也只是这一幅作品的具体 内容，并非他的招牌技能 B) ✓ 正确 turned one of Sao Paulo's transport tunnels into an amazing wall painting ↔ chose tunnels to do his graffiti art 预判要的是「他选了隧道做反向涂鸦」，chose tunnels to do his graffiti art 正是这层 客观事实的同义改写 C) 无中生有 suggested banning all polluting cars 文中无对应；Orion 的原话仅是批评驾驶者不顾 环境代价 they don't give any consideration to the price their comfort has for the environment，并未提出禁止任何污染车辆的建议 D) 以偏概全 was fond of doing creative artworks 把原文一次具体的隧道清洁创作扩大成「热衷于 做创意艺术品」这一普遍性格描述；原文 P2 只提到一次具体行动与一次发言，未对其 性格倾向作概括评价 作者对Leeds市议会的决定暗示了什么? A) 它简直荒谬。 B) 它是明智的。 C) 它相当出人意料。 D) 它相当合理。

questions.q: What does the author imply about Leeds City Council's decision?
options: It is simply absurd.
It is well-informed.
It is rather unexpected.
It is quite sensible.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author imply about Leeds City Council's decision? 中 imply 是推 断题的标志词，问作者对市议会决定的隐含态度

【拆句】题干 What does the author imply about Leeds City Council's decision? 是 What 引导 的特殊疑问句，主语 the author，谓语 imply，about 引导对象状语；imply 一词把本题定 性为推断题，是关键信号 49. What does the author imply about Leeds City Council's decision? A) It is simply absurd. B) It is well-informed. C) It is rather unexpected. D) It is quite sensible.

【定位】Moose was ordered to "clean up his act." How was he supposed to do this: by making all property he had cleaned dirty again? 穆斯被勒令「整改其行为」。他该怎么做呢：把他已经清洁过的所有地方再弄脏一遍？

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 How was he supposed to do this: by making all property he had cleaned dirty again? ↔ simply absurd 预判要的是「作者觉得这决定荒诞」，simply absurd 是该态度的最直接形容词替换 B) 与原文相反 well-informed（消息灵通、了解情况）是正面评价，与作者用归谬反问表达的否定态度 方向相反 C) 偷换概念 rather unexpected 把作者的「不合理、说不通」误写成「出乎意料」；原文并未表达 「我没想到他们会这么决定」，而是表达「这决定本身就站不住脚」 D) 与原文相反 quite sensible（相当明智）是正面评价，作者用归谬反问明显否定这一决定，方向相反 Sao Paulo市政官员如何处理Alexandre Orion的反向涂鸦? A) 他们让他清洁Sao Paulo所有的隧道。 B) 他们采取严厉措施禁止所有反向涂鸦。 C) 他们指控他污染城市隧道。 D) 他们使他无法进行艺术创作。

questions.q: How did Sao Paulo city officials handle Alexandre Orion's reverse graffiti?
options: They made him clean all the tunnels in Sao Paulo.
They took drastic action to ban all reverse graffiti.
They charged him with polluting tunnels in the city.
They made it impossible for him to practice his art.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 How did Sao Paulo city officials handle Alexandre Orion's reverse graffiti? 问官 方采取了什么客观行动，原文必有明文，按细节题处理

【拆句】题干 How did Sao Paulo city officials handle Alexandre Orion's reverse graffiti? 是 How 引导的特殊疑问句，handle 意为「处理、应对」；主体是官方，宾语是艺术家的作 品；结构清晰，无陷阱

【定位】The city officials then decided to take drastic action. They not only cleaned the whole tunnel but every tunnel in Sao Paulo. 市政官员随后决定采取激烈手段。他们不仅清洁了那条隧道，还清洁了圣保罗的每一条 隧道。 50. How did Sao Paulo city officials handle Alexandre Orion's reverse graffiti? A) They made him clean all the tunnels in Sao Paulo. B) They took drastic action to ban all reverse graffiti. C) They charged him with polluting tunnels in the city. D) They made it impossible for him to practice his art.

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 made him clean all the tunnels 把清洁主体偷换成艺术家本人；原文 They not only cleaned the whole tunnel 明确主语是 they（官方），不是艺术家 B) 过度推断 ban all reverse graffiti 把官方动作上升为「禁止反向涂鸦」的法规层面；原文 the authorities were annoyed but could find nothing to charge him with 明确说找不 到罪名，因此他们没有也无法颁布禁令，只是用清洁的方式釜底抽薪 C) 与原文相反 charged him with polluting tunnels 与原文明文 the authorities were annoyed but could find nothing to charge him with 直接矛盾——原文说「找不到罪名可控告」， 选项却说「以污染隧道为罪起诉了他」 D) ✓ 正确 They not only cleaned the whole tunnel but every tunnel in Sao Paulo ↔ made it impossible for him to practice his art The city officials then decided to take drastic action ↔ made it impossible for him to practice his art 预判要的是「让艺术家无法继续创作」，made it impossible for him to practice his art 正是该后果的客观表述；反向涂鸦的前提是脏面，官方清光所有脏面即从根本上让他 无法操作
